24: > This page applies to Unity IAP 5.4 and later only. Earlier versions of the IAP SDK don't collect any personal data. If you use an earlier version, refer to [Privacy overview for IAP versions earlier than 5.4](/iap/privacy-and-consent/legacy-overview.md).
25: 
26: ## Personal Data Collected about App Users/Game Players
27: 
28: Default Personal Data Collected (collected when a purchase flow runs, in order for the product to work):
29: 
30: * **Purchase and transaction information**, such as product, price, transaction details, and purchase data returned by the app store or payment provider
31: * **Device and application identifiers**, such as vendor or installation-specific identifiers and session identifiers
32: * **Device and technical information**, such as device model, OS version, language and locale
33: * **Approximate location** (country), which Unity's servers may derive from the IP address of incoming requests
34: 
35: Unity uses this data to run the IAP service, including deduplicating transactions, and to provide revenue reporting in the Unity Dashboard.
36: 
37: Optional Personal Data Collected (personal data which may be collected at choice/action of the end user/Developer):
38: 
39: * **Unity and developer-assigned identifiers**, such as installation, player, analytics, and user IDs, depending on the Unity services you initialize and the identifiers you set
40: * **Advertising identifiers**, such as advertising IDs (for example, IDFA and GAID) and Firebase identifiers, which are collected only when applicable ads consent is granted
41: * **Contact information**, such as an end user email address
42: * **Third-party identifiers**, such as analytics identifiers obtained if you have linked a third-party service
43: 
44: The categories above include examples only. The specific data elements collected may change over time and depend on your implementation and the features and services you enable.
45: 
46: On Unity 6000.7 and later, Unity IAP reports through the Editor's built-in Insights module, which also collects data classed as essential to its operation (session and app lifecycle events, device and OS attributes, and identifiers). This collection is governed by the [Developer Data Framework](/cloud/developer-data.md).
47: 
48: ### Developer-defined
49: 
50: While this product allows for the collection of developer defined data, we require that you not collect personal data through this mechanism. Our systems will not understand that it is personal data and so such would not be treated as such in retention processes or data subject requests.
51: 
52: ## Relationship under Privacy Laws
53: 
54: Depending on the processing activity, Unity handles your data in one of two roles:
55: 
56: * **As an independent controller** (European law) or **business** (California law) - Unity determines how and why the data is processed.
57: * **As your processor** (European law) or **service provider** (California law) - Unity processes the data on your behalf, with you acting as the controller or business.
58: 
59: > **Note:**
60: >
61: > To find which role applies to you and to Unity for a given activity, refer to [Unity's Data Processing Addendum](https://unity.com/legal/unity-data-processing-addendum-dpa) (**"DPA"**).
62: 
63: ## Legal Basis for Processing
64: 
65: Where Unity is a Processor, we do not determine the legal basis for processing. Instead, it is your responsibility as the Controller to determine such a legal basis.
66: 
67: In the limited circumstances in which Unity is an Independent Controller (refer to our [DPA](https://unity.com/legal/unity-data-processing-addendum-dpa)), you can find our legal basis for processing data collected through the IAP Service in our [Privacy Policy](https://unity.com/legal/game-player-and-app-user-privacy-policy). Please note: As an independent controller, you too should determine your own legal basis.
68: 
69: ## Consent (Opt in) vs Opt out
70: 
71: This product does not have its own consent service. Purchase events are sent regardless of the consent state, as they are required to operate the service. Consent affects only the advertising identifiers (including Firebase identifiers), which aren't collected when ads consent is denied through the Unity Consent API. If the Developer determines they need to obtain consent, or provide an opt-out, they must implement it client-side in a way determined by the developer.
72: 
73: ## Data Subject Requests
74: 
75: Two of the most common data subject requests based in law are the request for access to personal data and the request for deletion of personal data.
76: 
77: ### Access & Deletion Requests
78: 
79: How a data subject access or deletion request is handled depends on Unity's role in relation to the data:
80: 
81: * **Where Unity acts as a processor**, Unity actions requests only on your instruction. The request must therefore come from you, the developer — Unity will not action these requests if they are received directly from an end user.
82: * **Where Unity acts as a controller** (including as an independent controller), the request must come directly from the end user (the data subject).
83: 
84: At this time, the IAP Service has no native (self-serve) functionality to support these requests. Both processor instructions and controller requests are submitted through the **[IAP support form](https://support.unity.com/hc/en-us/requests/new?ticket_form_id=360001936712\&tf_360045015712=in-app_purchase__iap_)**, where Unity will manually action the request.
85: 
86: 1. Data for which Unity is a processor 
87: 
88:    This applies to:
89: 
90:    * Transaction data (except for CodaPay transaction data, see section below)
91:    * Other data you submit or generate through the IAP service
92: 
93:    You are responsible for receiving and validating requests from your end users and then instructing Unity to action them. Submit your instruction through the support form linked above.
94: 
95: 2. Data for which Unity is a controller 
96: 
97:    The end user must contact Unity directly by using the support form linked above:
98: 
99:    * Webshop account login data
100:    * CodaPay transaction data
101:      * Unity, Developer and CodaPay operate as independent controllers
102:    * Transaction and billing data used for Unity's own purposes — Unity is an independent controller where it uses this data for its own legitimate business purposes, including internal financial reporting and auditing, complying with legal and regulatory obligations; and security monitoring and fraud prevention. Requests relating to this processing come directly from the end user.
103: 
104: > **Note:**
105: >
106: > The same transaction records may be both processed on your behalf (Section 1) and used by Unity as an independent controller (Section 2). The two roles are distinct, and requests are routed according to the role engaged.
107: 
108: ## Dependencies
109: 
110: ### Unity Product Dependencies
111: 
112: * Unity Authentication SDK: Unity IAP uses Authentication only if your project already includes it. Refer to [Unity Authentication SDK](/authentication.md) for more information.
113: 
114: ### Payment Dependencies
115: 
116: Platform payment processing:
117: 
118: If you distribute through the Apple App Store or Google Play, payments are processed at the platform level under each platform's terms.
119: 
120: * **Apple App Store** — Refer to the Apple App Store terms.
121: * **Google Play** — Refer to the Google Play terms.
122: 
123: Payment providers:
124: 
125: You can choose to enable a payment provider. When you do, you enter into your own agreement directly with that provider, which governs your use of their service.
126: 
127: ## Personal Data Retention
128: 
129: Device details are fetched by the SDK each time it sends a purchase event and held only in memory until they're forwarded to Unity. Transaction data is kept in the IAP service for as long as it's needed to run the service for your project. For native store purchases, the transaction ID is retained to prevent processing the same purchase twice and for IAP revenue reporting. Configs and OAuth tokens are retained until you delete them.
130: 
131: IAP service logs are kept for 30 days.
132: 
133: ## Child Privacy
134: 
135: If required to do so under applicable laws, you (the developer) must obtain verifiable parental consent prior to submitting child-user data as outlined in the [Unity Terms of Service](https://unity.com/legal/terms-of-service) through the IAP Service which includes the Webshop Service.
136: 
137: If your app is in the Apple App Store Kids Category, refer to [Build for the Apple Kids Category](/iap/apple-kids-category.md) to leave the AdSupport framework and the code that reads the advertising identifier (IDFA) out of your iOS and tvOS builds.
138: 
139: ## Privacy Policy Requirements
140: 
141: It is never appropriate to use Unity’s privacy policy for your application. You will need to ensure that the personal data practices are reflected in your Privacy Policy, as required in the [Unity Terms of Service](https://unity.com/legal/terms-of-service).
142: 
143: ## Privacy URL
144: 
145: If you need to present the user with Unity’s privacy policy or reference it within your own, use the privacy URL: [https://unity.com/legal/game-player-and-app-user-privacy-policy](https://unity.com/legal/game-player-and-app-user-privacy-policy).

1: # Changelog
2: 
3: All notable changes to this package will be documented in this file.
4: 
5: The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](http://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/)
6: and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](http://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
7: 
8: ## [1.19.0] - 2026-11-03
9: 
10: ### Added
11: - Services CLI commands for Core (`Cli/`, compiled only when `com.unity.pipeline` is installed) now ship with the package.
12: - Live Releases: choose a release for each environment in Project Settings > Services > Environments, or set a release pointer at runtime with `InitializationOptions.SetReleasePointer`. On Unity 6000.4 and newer, build profiles can also select a release pointer. The selected release is exposed to other Unity Gaming Services packages through Core.
13: - Live Releases: the active release selection is now saved per environment, so switching environments restores each environment's previously chosen release.
14: 
15: ### Changed
16: - When no active environment is set after refreshing the environment list, the editor now automatically selects 'production' as the default.
17: - `UnityServices.ExternalUserId` now delegates to the engine's
18:   `UnityEngine.Identifiers.Identifiers.userId` API when the engine
19:   supports it.
20: - Added newly required `[NoAutoStaticsCleanup]` for support on Unity 6.7+
21: 
22: ### Fixed
23: - Fixed a compilation error on .NET 8+ (`SYSLIB0051`) caused by `InvalidJwtException`'s legacy serialization constructor; the constructor is now marked obsolete on those runtimes.
24: - Packages that require components from a package that failed to initialize are no longer
25:   initialized, so a failure such as an unlinked project ID is no longer accompanied by misleading
26:   "There is no component registered. Are you missing a package?" errors.
27: - Live Releases: the Editor no longer requests release pointers or releases before the project ID is available (early in a session before the project link resolves, or in a headless Editor). These requests logged a misleading 'Failed to fetch release pointers (404)' warning. The lists are fetched once the project ID arrives. Release fetch warnings now include the request path, and HTTP failures fetching releases are now logged.

1: # Changelog
2: ## [5.5.1] - 2026-11-13
3: ### Changed
4: - Updated the `com.unity.services.core` dependency to 1.19.0, which fixes "Attempted to get location for assembly Unity.Services.Core.Editor ... while it is unloading" being logged on every domain reload under CoreCLR.
5: - Authoring - Deploying a routing config (`.iaprouting`) now reads the routing on the server first and names the tags that the deploy removes because the file doesn't have them, also on a dry run. A failed read now fails the deploy instead of overwriting routing that was never read. The `enforceProviderTagValidation` field is no longer sent, as the server never used it; files that still have it load as before.
6: - Samples - Updated the samples to use `PurchasingController` instead of `StoreController` and the individual store, product and purchase services.
7: 
8: ### Fixed
9: - Authoring - Fixed a `403 Forbidden` error logged on every domain reload since 5.5.0 when ProjectSettings has a cloud project ID that isn't linked, or that the signed-in user can't access. Comparing catalog items against their remote counterpart is now skipped when the project isn't linked or has no catalog items. If the project's environments can't be loaded, the reason now shows as the items' status in the Deployment window instead of as a Console error.
10: - Authoring - A pending wait for the project to be linked to a cloud project no longer keeps the catalog deployment objects alive across a code reload, which leaked under CoreCLR.
11: - Google Play - `UpgradeDowngradeSubscription(Product, Product, GooglePlayReplacementMode)` no longer fails with "Sequence contains no matching element" when the old subscription isn't among the fetched purchases. It now falls back to the old product's transaction id.
12: - Insights - Purchase and session events now include the Firebase session ID when one is available and allowed. It was collected when consented to, but left out of the event sent to Unity, so it never reached Unity's purchase data.
13: - Remote catalog - Products could be missing from the remote catalog and from Payment Provider products when the environment holds more than 100 configs, because fetching stopped at the first page with fewer than 100 items. Fetching now continues until the server reports no more items.
14: 
15: ## [5.5.0] - 2026-11-04
16: ### Added
17: - Added `Order.StoreName` and `Product.StoreName`, the name of the store an order belongs to or a product was fetched from.
18: - Added `PurchasingController`, which drives several stores (for example Google Play and a Payment Provider) from one object. Calls apply to every store unless a `storeName` is passed, and calls that take a `Product` or `Order` go to its `StoreName`.
19: - Added `IOrderInfo.PurchaseDate`, the UTC date and time of the purchase. It is `null` when the store does not provide one, for a `DeferredOrder`, and for a `FailedOrder` that was not a pending order first.
20: - Apple - Added `IAppleStoreExtendedService.ClearTransactionLog(bool debugOnly)`, which can also clear the transaction log in release builds. `ClearTransactionLog()` is now obsolete.
21: - Apple - Added the `IAP_DISABLE_IDFA` scripting define symbol for apps in the Kids Category. When set, iOS and tvOS builds leave out the AdSupport framework and the code that reads the advertising identifier (IDFA). Developers remain responsible for their own child-directed designation and for any other SDKs in their app.
22: - Authoring - Catalog items have an optional purchase limit (count per hour, day or month) in the inspector and as the `PurchaseLimitCount` and `PurchaseLimitPeriod` `.catalog.csv` columns. Catalog items are now deployed with the `UnityRemoteCatalog` 1.2.0 schema.
23: - Payment Providers - Added `IPaymentProvidersExtendedService.GetPurchaseEligibility`, which returns whether the player can buy each catalog listing now, how many purchases remain, and when the limit resets.
24: - Payment Providers - Added `PaymentProviderProductMetadata.purchaseLimit`, which exposes a catalog listing's purchase limit (`count` per `PurchaseLimitPeriod` of `Hour`, `Day` or `Month`). It is null when the listing has no limit.
25: - Payment Providers - Added `PurchaseFailureReason.PurchaseLimitReached`. A purchase that would exceed the catalog listing's purchase limit now fails with this reason instead of `ExistingPurchasePending` or `DuplicateTransaction`.
26: - Payment Providers - Added `StoreController.PaymentProvidersExtendedService`, named like the other extended services. Update calls to `StoreController.PaymentProviderStoreExtendedService` to use the new name; the old name will be removed in a future major version.
27: 
28: ### Changed
29: - Apple - Updated the Apple privacy manifest ([PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/iap/privacy-and-consent/apple-privacy-manifest#privacyinfo.xcprivacy)) with the data the SDK collects.
30: - Authoring - Comparing catalog items against their remote counterpart now only reports differences. A matching item no longer shows "Up to date", which could become stale when the remote changed afterwards; an item showing "Deployed" keeps that status unless a difference is found.
31: - Editor - Redesigned the In-App Purchasing settings page, with "Cloud setup" and "AI Skills" tabs and cards for each store and payment provider.
32: 
33: ### Fixed
34: - A `PendingOrder` that arrives while `OnPurchasePending` has no subscriber is no longer treated as handled. The next `FetchPurchases` after subscribing sends it to `OnPurchasePending`. Previously it was not sent there again until the next launch.
35: - AI skill - The skill now points to the [Platform compliance](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/iap/platform-compliance) guidance.
36: - Apple (StoreKit 2) - `ConfirmPurchase` now reports a `FailedOrder` through `OnPurchaseConfirmed` when StoreKit cannot finish the transaction (for example, while offline), after trying three times. That transaction now stays pending and is redelivered on launch matching the behavior of the other stores.
37: - Apple (StoreKit 2) - Fixed pending transactions that could not be finished. Confirming a `PendingOrder` now finishes its transaction even when StoreKit no longer lists it as unfinished.
38: - Apple - Clearing the transaction log no longer throws a `DirectoryNotFoundException` when nothing has been recorded yet or the log was already cleared.
39: - Apple - The App Receipt in `order.Info.Receipt` is now always up to date.
40:   - `IAppleStoreExtendedPurchaseService.SetRefreshAppReceipt` is `true` by default again.
41: - Apple - The store now starts listening for transactions only once products are fetched and `OnPurchasePending` has a subscriber. Purchases left unfinished from an earlier session are now delivered to `OnPurchasePending` when the game subscribes, instead of being delivered to no one right after `FetchProducts`. On StoreKit 1, `RestoreTransactions` called before that now fails right away with a message, instead of never completing.
42: - Editor - Fixed an `AssemblyLoadContext` leaking on every code reload under CoreCLR.
43: - Editor - Without a domain reload, a Play session no longer reuses the Payment Provider, webshop, live content and catalog clients of an earlier session, which kept that session's access token, environment and project. Session events are sent again in every Play session, not only the first.
44: - Editor - Without a domain reload, Developer Data settings changed in the Unity Dashboard are now picked up in the next Play session.
45: - Fixed Nintendo Switch 2 player builds failing when the In-App Purchasing package is installed.
46: - Google Play - A consumable that was already consumed is no longer reported through `OnPurchasePending` again when a device with a stale Play cache returns it after the app restarts. Previously it came back on every launch and could never be confirmed.
47: - Payment Providers - On iPad, a purchase made in the external browser is no longer cancelled when the browser opens in a window overlapping the game. The game briefly regained focus, which cancelled the order while the player was still paying.
48: - Payment Providers - The Purchase Options UI keeps its rounded backgrounds, button colours and payment brand logos when entering Play Mode again without a domain reload. Previously, every Play session after the first drew flat rectangles and generic options until the next domain reload.
49: - Remote catalog - Calling `RemoteCatalogProvider.FetchRemoteCatalog` again no longer duplicates every product; it replaces the previous catalog, and leaves it empty if the fetch fails.
50: - Xbox - macOS and Linux player builds no longer fail with `XGamingRuntime` compile errors when "Build for Microsoft GDK" is enabled.
51: 
52: ## [5.4.4] - 2026-10-02
53: ### Added
54: - Added a dependency on `com.unity.services.deployment`, so the Deployment window is available for deploying catalog items without installing it separately.
55: - Authoring - Newly created `.ucat` files include a `$schema` reference for editor and CLI validation.
56: - Editor - Added a button to migrate a codeless product catalog to the Remote Catalog, on the In-App Purchasing settings page and in the IAP Catalog window.
57: - GooglePlay - Android builds now log a warning when no Google Play license key is set in the cloud project settings, or when the project isn't linked to a cloud project.
58: - Payment Providers - Added `ProductDescription.catalogListingId` and a `ProductDescription(string, ProductMetadata, string)` constructor that sets it, so a store whose catalog listings share a store-specific id can describe each listing with its own metadata.
59: 
60: ### Changed
61: - Authoring - `.catalog.csv` columns are now derived from the catalog item model itself, so a property added to a catalog item appears in CSV without a parsing change, and the Editor and the UGS CLI pick the columns up from the same place. Column order, cell formatting and the warnings reported for a malformed file are unchanged.
62: - Editor - Codeless In-App Purchasing is closed to new projects. *Services > In-App Purchasing > Create IAP Button*, *Create IAP Listener* and *IAP Catalog* are available only in a project that already has a legacy catalog, and the "IAP Catalog..." button has been removed from the IAP Button inspector. Existing `CodelessIAPButton` and `IAPListener` components keep working, and a project using codeless keeps its menu items.
63: - Editor - The In-App Purchasing settings page presents the local catalog as a legacy one. The section is titled "Legacy Catalog", it appears only when the project has an existing legacy catalog to migrate, and its button reads "Migrate to Remote Catalog" rather than opening the catalog editor.
64: - Editor - Android store stripping now runs once per player build through a build callback, rather than once per scene through `[PostProcessScene]`. It no longer runs on entering Play Mode.
65: 
66: ### Fixed
67: - A `FailedOrder` reported through `OnPurchaseConfirmed` now carries the `Info` (receipt, transaction ID) of the `PendingOrder` passed to `ConfirmPurchase`.
68: - Analytics - Apple (StoreKit 2) - Fixed transaction data reported to Unity Analytics for revenue validation.
69: - Apple - Fixed a main-actor violation under Swift 6 strict concurrency, where native entry points with no guaranteed thread performed reads that are only valid on the main thread.
70: - Apple (StoreKit 2) - Fixed the introductory offer data. It is now properly returned in `GetProductDetails` and `GetIntroductoryPriceDictionary`. Both now also include an `isEligibleForIntroOffer` field indicating whether the user can redeem the offer.
71: - Apple - `GetProductDetails` and `GetIntroductoryPriceDictionary` now keep products from every fetch instead of only the most recent one. Previously, fetching additional products replaced the previously fetched ones in these dictionaries.
72:   - These products are now cleared before the `OnAuthAccountChanged` event is raised, and only when that event has a subscriber; a product fetch in flight at that moment is failed instead of caching the previous account's results.
73: - Apple - `bool` values returned from native code are now marshalled as a single byte, matching Objective-C `BOOL` and Swift `Bool`. The default marshalling reads four bytes, so the three unused bytes could make a native `false` surface as `true` in `IAppleExtensions.canMakePayments`.
74: - Apple (StoreKit 2) - Fixed intermittent multi-minute delays in product fetches, purchases, and other StoreKit operations while the app was under load, most noticeable on older devices.
75: - Apple - Callbacks passed to native code are now kept alive for the lifetime of the process. The previous code relied on garbage collector behaviour that does not hold under CoreCLR, which is available as an experimental build option in 6000.7. Projects using the default Mono scripting backend are unaffected.
76: - Apple - Google Analytics identifiers are collected for iOS and tvOS when Google Analytics is linked, or when Developer Data Collection is set to Recommended, in addition to the existing end-user ads consent requirement. Configure this in the Unity Dashboard, under Project Settings > Developer Data.
77: - Apple (StoreKit 2) - Fixed a purchase being reported twice when `Transaction.updates` delivered it separately from its `purchase()` call's answer. If the updates delivery came first and the purchase was confirmed before the answer arrived, the answer failed with a spurious `PurchaseFailureReason.DuplicateTransaction`; otherwise `OnPurchasePending` fired a second time. Each purchase is now reported once, whichever copy arrives first; other transactions delivered during a purchase, such as a subscription renewal, are still reported immediately.
78: - Authoring - A `.catalog.csv` cell that can't be read is now reported once per row rather than once per read, and a numeric `ProductType`, `Language` or `PromotionType` cell outside the values those types define is reported instead of being stored as a value with no name.
79: - Authoring - Fixed an exception when leaving a catalog item inspector with unsaved changes.
80: - GooglePlay - Fixed an `ArgumentNullException` when Google Play reports a purchase update with no purchase in flight (e.g. when a cancelled subscription's active period expires) and no product id is known; the failure is now reported with an `UnknownProduct` placeholder product.
81: - Payment Providers - The country, currency and locale sent when creating checkout and webshop sessions are now read from the device's OS settings (natively on Windows, macOS, Android, iOS, tvOS and visionOS) instead of .NET `System.Globalization`, which reported `en-US`/`US`/`USD` for many locales regardless of the OS region. Store-provided storefront data still takes precedence when available.
82: - Payment Providers - On iOS, fetching the App Store storefront via `ExternalPurchaseClient.FetchStorefrontAsync` now also applies the storefront country, and on iOS 17 and later its currency, to subsequent Payment Provider orders. The currency also needs Xcode 16.3 or newer at build time, and is omitted on older toolchains.
83: - Payment Providers - For products with multiple `Product.catalogListings` entries, each catalog listing now shows its own metadata and price, matching what checkout charges.
84:   - Purchase Options UI - Discount badges and the webshop option now use the selected catalog listing.
85:   - Orders returned after checkout and from `FetchPurchases` now report the catalog listing that was bought, instead of the product's base listing.
86: - Payment Providers - Catalog listing titles and descriptions now fall back to an entry matching the player's language (e.g. `en-NG` → `en-US`) before defaulting to the first available entry.
87: 
88: ## [5.4.3] - 2026-09-03
89: ### Added
90: - Authoring - Payment Provider Routing files (`.iaprouting`) can now be created and deployed from the Unity Editor Deployment Window.
91: - Authoring - Added validation preventing deployment of catalog items whose store-specific product ID overrides conflict across different SKUs. Per-item validation also catches empty override values and duplicate store entries.
92: - Google Analytics identifiers are collected when Google Analytics is linked, or when Developer Data Collection is set to Recommended, in addition to the existing end-user ads consent requirement. Configure this in the Unity Dashboard, under Project Settings > Developer Data.
93: - GooglePlay - Added `IGoogleOrderInfo.OrderId` (accessible via `Order.Info.Google.OrderId`), exposing the Google Play order id of a purchase ([`Purchase.getOrderId()`](https://developer.android.com/reference/com/android/billingclient/api/Purchase#getOrderId())).
94: - GooglePlay - Added `IGoogleOrderInfo.PurchaseToken`, exposing the Google Play purchase token under its own name. This returns the same value as `IOrderInfo.TransactionID`, which contains the purchase token on Google Play.
95: - Authoring - When catalog items (`.ucat` or `catalog.csv`) are changed, they will now be compared to their remote counterpart if it exists. 
96: 
97: ### Changed
98: - Insights - On Unity 6000.7.0a7 and newer, the package uses the Editor's built-in Insights module to report IAP telemetry. Activating the module also collects data classed as essential to its operation, including session and app lifecycle events, device and OS attributes, and identifiers that associate telemetry with a project and session. Collection is governed by Unity's [Developer Data framework](https://docs.unity.com/cloud/en-us/developer-data-framework/overview) and can be managed per project in the Diagnostics section of Project Settings. On older Editor versions, the package reports through the existing gateway, unchanged.
99: - Authoring - `.ucat` catalog files now serialize store ID overrides as flat fields (`googleOverride`, `appleOverride`, `xboxStoreOverride`, `macAppStoreOverride`) instead of the `storeIdOverrides` array. Existing files with the array format are still read correctly.
100: - Remote Catalog - Runtime catalog requests now use the project-scoped Live Content domain.
101: - Updated the link to the Apple Developer Program License Agreement in [Third Party Notices](./Third%20Party%20Notices.md).
102: 
103: ### Fixed
104: - Catalog - `CatalogProvider` no longer applies another store's product ID override to stores that have none. Products with an override for only some stores (e.g. Apple but not Google) now correctly fall back to the default product ID on the other stores.
105: - Catalog - The legacy `UnityPurchasing.Initialize` path now resolves the running store before fetching products. Previously it used whichever store-specific product ID was registered last, so a product configured with `ConfigurationBuilder.AddProduct` for more than one store could be fetched using another store's ID. Products with an override for a single store were unaffected.
106: - GooglePlay - Fixed OrderInfo.Receipt's price_amount_micros returning a string instead of a long.
107: - GooglePlay - Confirming a `PendingOrder` that Google Play has already acknowledged now triggers `OnPurchaseConfirmed` with a `PurchaseFailureReason.DuplicateTransaction` `FailedOrder`. Previously `OnPurchaseConfirmed` was not triggered at all. This applies to `ProductType.NonConsumable`, `ProductType.Subscription` and `ProductType.Unknown` products, and can happen when the purchase was acknowledged by your backend or on another device.
108: - GooglePlay - `FetchPurchases` and `RestoreTransactions` silently dropped purchases whose products had never been fetched; these are now returned as unknown products.
109: - GooglePlay - Fixed Android builds failing with `Execution failed for task ':launcher:checkReleaseDuplicateClasses'` on specific Unity Editor versions.
110: - GooglePlay - Fixed `AndroidJavaObject` references causing a memory leak when fetching products.
111: - Editor Play Mode - Fixed slow Play Mode entry on projects with many assets by skipping Android store configuration outside of player builds.
112: - Apple - Fixed additional Swift 6 strict concurrency data race errors in `TransactionObserverUseCase`, `TransactionUseCase`, and `UnityPurchasingInAppBrowserController` that caused build failures when `SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY` is set to `complete`.
113: - Apple - Purchasing now uses the product cached at fetch time instead of re-fetching it from the App Store on every purchase call.
114: - Apple - Product lookup errors at purchase time (e.g. network failures) are now reported with their real error message instead of being misreported as `PurchaseFailureReason.ProductUnavailable`.
115: - Apple - `FailedOrder`s with `PurchaseFailureReason.DuplicateTransaction` reported through `OnPurchaseFailed` now carry the order's `Info` (including `TransactionID`) instead of an empty `OrderInfo`, so the failure can be attributed to the transaction it concerns.
